platform-overview.title: The platform
platform-overview.summary: ~21 containers, one schema, human approval gates on everything that ships.

sections.problem: Running real AI pipelines against real personal data needs more than API keys: it needs a data layer, network isolation, and controls that survive automation.
sections.solution: Self-hosted Supabase (Postgres 15, Kong, GoTrue, Realtime, Storage) as the single source of truth. Multi-tenant schema from day one: UUID keys, user_id plus RLS on every table. Two production applications on top: a job-search command center and a document-rendering microservice.
implementation: One heavily customized docker-compose runs the fleet on a 4 vCPU / 8GB VPS.
Cloudflare Tunnel + Access in front of admin surfaces; Docker-internal DNS everywhere.
House rule: no LLM for anything mechanical. Sorting, staleness, search, and analytics are pure computation.
sections.iteration: Every later release in this changelog ran through the same gates: written spec, plan review, my approval, measured verification, my push.

muchane-com.title: This site: zero dependencies on purpose
muchane-com.summary: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no remote scripts. The rejections are the design.

sections.problem: A portfolio claiming engineering judgment shouldn't ship a framework payload to render a star map.
sections.solution: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS with zero build step and zero remote script origins. The rejection ledger is the point: no frameworks, no GSAP (WAAPI covers the zoom), no WebGL (Canvas 2D covers the starfield), each rejected for a stated reason rather than by taste.
implementation: Path-based routing: hard render on direct load, animated zoom on click-through; back pops one zoom level.
Dependency-free circular carousel; satellite orbits with derived geometry and clearance proofs.
85 test ids shipped ahead of the E2E suite rebuild.
sections.iteration: An 8-commit refinement pass plus a 6-commit fix pass (Aug 12–13, 2026). Light mode removed: a starfield does not survive inversion.

tailoring-quality-triad.title: Tailoring under control: grounding, growth caps, model-per-task
tailoring-quality-triad.summary: Three controls shipped together so tailored documents can't invent claims or bloat past two pages.

sections.problem: Three failure modes in AI document tailoring: models invent qualifications, tailored text silently bloats a canonical 2-page resume onto page 3, and one model for everything either overspends or underperforms by subtask.
sections.solution: Three independent controls. Claim-grounding: a verification model at temperature 0 checks every proposed edit against my real profile; ungrounded claims are dropped, overclaims are kept but flagged for my review. That asymmetry is deliberate: fabrication is auto-rejected, exaggeration is a human judgment call. Growth ledger: per-bullet caps plus a document ceiling, so tailoring is reallocation, not accretion. Model-per-task: a cheap model generates, a stronger model evaluates.
implementation: Document growth mathematically bounded at +78 characters against a 6,360-character budget: no combination of legal per-bullet growth can breach the page limit.
Evaluator selection was empirical: models compared on score-band placement (6 distinct output values vs. compressed bands), not vibes.
Nothing is ever submitted automatically. Every document gets human review.
sections.iteration: A standing finding from the evals: the fit score measures resume-to-job fit, not tailoring quality, and honest paraphrase should not move an honest evaluator. That distinction now shapes what the pipeline is allowed to claim about itself.

paragraph-break-overlap.title: The 16% that never rendered
paragraph-break-overlap.summary: Edits spanning a paragraph break logged as applied but never rendered. A sixth of output, silently discarded.

sections.problem: The renderer resolved each tailoring edit against pristine base text. Edits spanning a paragraph break silently failed: logged as applied, absent from the shipped document. Measured across the prior corpus, ~16% of "applied" edits had never rendered. Paid model output, thrown away invisibly.
sections.solution: A crossesBreak check with strict inequality, run before slot occupancy, rejects any spanning edit so it regenerates within bounds. Rejected alternative: teaching the renderer to apply cross-break edits. Constraining generation is simpler than complicating application semantics.
implementation: Boundary math validated in the ops layer before any write.
Two verification executions confirmed first-attempt renders, zero retries.
The diagnostic matters: structural log comparison was blind to the failure. Only walking the corpus with field extraction exposed it.
sections.iteration: The investigation exposed a contaminated control set: "applied" labels included pre-strip operations, so the known-good corpus didn't prove what it claimed. Kept as a rule: interrogate what a good label actually attests.

companies-surface.title: /companies: intelligence, funnel, and staleness in one surface
companies-surface.summary: ~70 tracked companies with pure-SQL analytics. No analytics service, no ETL copy.

sections.problem: Research, postings, applications, and comp data spread across tables, with no single answer to: where do I stand with this company, is my intel stale, where do applications die in the funnel.
sections.solution: One surface: target cards in a carousel, tabbed detail pages, and an Analytics tab computed entirely in SQL against the live schema. Staleness is measured, not guessed: a company_views table records every look, under RLS.
implementation: Funnel with time-in-stage, response rate, posting velocity, comp bands, fit-dimension distribution: all pure SQL.
Test suite grew 719 → 835 vitest and 87 → 103 Playwright specs, 0 failures.
A rail-layout defect traced to duplicated breakpoint values; the breakpoint was hoisted into a single exported constant.
sections.iteration: The fit-score slot shipped null-tolerant so the surface renders before the upstream score exists. Display first, data later.

ats-ingestion-feed-complete.title: Ingestion that closes its own ghosts
ats-ingestion-feed-complete.summary: Adapter-per-ATS on staggered 4-hour schedules, with an invariant that makes lifecycle closure safe.

sections.problem: Two hard problems in multi-ATS ingestion: dedup without fake placeholder keys (Postgres treats NULL != NULL), and closure: marking a posting dead requires knowing the feed you just read was complete. A partial feed treated as complete mass-closes live postings.
sections.solution: Adapters per source feeding a shared core, with an explicit invariant: any trigger path that is not a complete company feed must set feed_complete=false, or the core will close everything it didn't see. Rejected alternative: per-posting liveness checks, O(postings) requests against rate-limited vendors.
implementation: Greenhouse every 4h (~1,949 postings per cycle, full content), Ashby offset 10 minutes, retention sweep after: staggered for a 4-vCPU box.
Sequential batch processing before dedup checks prevents race-condition duplicates.
A designed Lever adapter extends the invariant with a sentinel-probe completeness gate: prove the feed is complete before it may close anything.
sections.iteration: The invariant became system law: a planned single-URL ingest path is designed around it, forced to declare its feeds incomplete. No mass-close incidents on record since.

updated-at-phantom-writer.title: Hunting a phantom writer
updated-at-phantom-writer.summary: updated_at churned on every cycle. The writer wasn't on the table being written.

sections.problem: updated_at on jobs rows churned every ingestion cycle even when nothing changed, poisoning staleness logic and masking real updates. The jobs table's own triggers and write paths were clean.
sections.solution: Widen the search: inventory triggers on every table that writes into the target, not just the target. The writer was a trigger on the job_locations junction table, touching the parent row on every location re-upsert. Dropped, and all write paths now diff before writing.
implementation: A second latent bug fixed in the same pass: the update mapping was NULL-writing two score columns on every cycle.
Diff-before-write adopted as the standard for every update path.
sections.iteration: The junction-table lesson is now a standing diagnostic rule, and the repaired timestamp feeds the /companies staleness chips with a signal worth trusting.

kanban-status-history.title: Kanban with measured time-in-stage
kanban-status-history.summary: A DB trigger writes every status transition to an append-only history table, so funnel analytics compute from real events, not a mutable column.

dual-path-network.title: Two paths to one database
dual-path-network.summary: App traffic rides Kong under JWT-enforced RLS. Automation rides an isolated internal network. The tiers can't reach each other.

sections.problem: The automation engine needs upsert semantics the REST layer cannot express: multi-column conflict resolution on nullable keys, where Postgres evaluates NULL != NULL and matching fails outright. The naive fixes are all bad: placeholder sentinels pollute the schema; exposing Postgres to the app tier widens the attack surface.
sections.solution: Two physically separate data paths. Application traffic: Nginx Proxy Manager to Kong to services, JWT-enforced Row Level Security, apps see only their user's rows. System traffic: n8n direct to Postgres over an internal Docker bridge the web-facing proxy has no route to. Rejected: routing automation through PostgREST (can't express the writes). Rejected: sentinel values (dishonest schema).
implementation: Port 5432 never exposed publicly; system traffic never leaves the internal bridge.
Services addressed by Docker-internal DNS, never IPs.
Codified convention: Postgres nodes for writes, Supabase nodes for simple reads, sequential batches before dedup checks.
A compromised frontend cannot reach the database port. Different tier.
sections.iteration: Every later pipeline (ingestion, research, tailoring) shipped without needing a new network path. The NULL lesson became a standing rule: check existence before upserting on nullable fields.

char-budget-gate.title: Stop asking LibreOffice how many pages a Word document has
char-budget-gate.summary: Identity round-trip testing proved the renderer miscounts the unmodified template. The page gate became a character budget.

sections.problem: The document renderer gated output on LibreOffice's page count. Identity round-trip testing proved LibreOffice counts the 2-page Calibri template as 3 pages even with genuine Microsoft Calibri installed, so the gate rejected valid documents. A compounding bug: the spec endpoint reported a budget equal to the base length, telling the tailoring model it had zero room to expand.
sections.solution: Replace page counting with a character budget: a per-template sidecar declares canonical pages and a hard budget (6,360 characters for the primary template). Rejected alternative: chasing font-metric parity inside LibreOffice. The identity test showed the renderer disagrees with Word on the untouched template itself, so no amount of tuning converges.
implementation: Balanced bold markers stripped before counting so formatting doesn't consume budget.
Error-response shape preserved for the pipeline consumer; new diagnostic fields added (actual chars, budget, per-field breakdown).
44/44 pytest tests pass in-container.
sections.iteration: The diagnostic fields later made retry accounting debuggable, and the budget concept moved upstream in August as the growth ledger: constrain generation, not just output.

n8n-bloat-surgery.title: 3.65GB of dead execution logs
n8n-bloat-surgery.summary: The automation engine was persisting full execution data for every successful run, and the backups were hauling it.

sections.problem: Full execution data persisted for every successful run of three high-frequency ingestion workflows: 3.65GB on an 8GB VPS, with the backup pipeline compressing and shipping ~3.36GB of dead logs every cycle.
sections.solution: Success-execution retention set to none on the three ingestion workflows, keeping failure data for debugging. Rejected alternative: periodic manual pruning, a treadmill that fails open the week nobody runs it.
implementation: Data volume 3.65GB → 72.75MB, ~98% reduction; backup archives ~3.36GB → ~385MB compressed.
The exemption that matters was verified, not assumed: a manual test execution was fired specifically to prove hand-run debugging still captures full data.
sections.iteration: The verification step is the story: positive evidence of the behavior you need, not absence of the behavior you don't.

agent-hardening.title: A locked-down user for the coding agent
agent-hardening.summary: The VPS coding agent runs as a dedicated no-sudo user with command blocks, a logged network wrapper, and session and incident logs. Autonomy inside enforced guardrails, not trust.

swap-provisioning.title: Swap before the OOM killer wins
swap-provisioning.summary: Diagnosed the VPS running with zero swap and the OOM killer firing immediately under pressure. 4GB provisioned; ~2GB in steady use.

backup-integrity.title: Backups that restore, not backups that exist
backup-integrity.summary: A PTY flag was corrupting dumps in transit. Dropped; historical dumps tested individually; verified-restore roadmap in place.

workflow-status-lights.title: Green and amber lights
workflow-status-lights.summary: Every pipeline upserts a heartbeat row to workflow_runs, surfaced as status lights in the app footer. Health at a glance, not at failure.
